summary: Cross-solver findings bus is inert: normal exits never populate `findings_summary`
detail: The swarm posts to the message bus only when `result.findings_summary` is non-empty (backend/agents/swarm.py:334-337), but `_findings` is assigned only on the error/no-tools path (486, 503) and the rescue paths (510, 513, 538) — a normal `return self._result(GAVE_UP)` (489) always carries `findings_summary=""`, and the FLAG_FOUND path is typically empty too. Consequently `check_findings()` can only ever answer "No new findings", and `bump()` always receives the fallback "No sibling insights available yet." (swarm.py:169): the sibling knowledge sharing that docs/rewrite-plan.md §4 keeps is a no-op in practice.
fix_hint: Capture a bounded progress note (recent tool outcomes / last model text) into `_findings` before returning GAVE_UP/FLAG_FOUND so the bus and bump carry real content.

summary: `asyncio.CancelledError` is swallowed and converted into a normal return, breaking cancellation semantics for any supervisor
detail: `except asyncio.CancelledError: ... return self._result(CANCELLED, cancel_reason=reason)` (491-500) absorbs the cancellation instead of re-raising it. Consequences: `task.cancel(); await task` returns a value instead of raising, `task.cancelled()` is False, `asyncio.timeout()` never raises TimeoutError when its inner coroutine absorbs the cancel, and anyio cancel scopes / TaskGroup-adjacent supervision cannot observe shutdown. The current swarm tolerates it (it drives cancellation through `cancel_event` plus shields), but the solver silently defeats the standard asyncio contract it is embedded in.
fix_hint: After recording state (including the confirmed-flag check), re-`raise` the CancelledError; let the caller map it to a SolverResult if needed (e.g. wrap the await in `_run_solver` and catch there).
evidence: Code behavior is as claimed: headless_solver.py:491-500 catches asyncio.CancelledError and runs `return self._result(CANCELLED, cancel_reason=reason)` without re-raising, so a task.cancel()'ed solver task completes with a value and task.cancelled() is False. However, every in-repo supervisor is cancellation-tolerant (swarm.py:454-456 `p.cancel(); await asyncio.gather(*pending, return_exceptions=True)`; coordinator_core.py:184-189 re-raises at the swarm layer), no asyncio.timeout/anyio cancel scope wraps the solver, and the conversion is deliberate (comment at :493-495). Real contract violation but latent-only in this codebase -> severity corrected to low.

summary: Step accounting is a shared-mutable-list hack mutated from three modules and introspected via getattr
detail: `self._step_count = [0]` (369) is mutated by TracingToolset (backend/agents/tracing_toolset.py:37), by the rescue path (`self._step_count[0] += 1`, line 518), and read back through private introspection in the swarm: `getattr(getattr(solver, "_step_count", None), "__getitem__", lambda _: 0)(0)` (swarm.py:507). Rescue submissions inflate "steps" that measure neither model turns nor tool calls, the web progress estimate derived from it is meaningless, and any refactor to a real counter object silently degrades swarm status output to 0.
fix_hint: Expose a proper property/method (`steps`, `progress()`) on the solver incremented only by the toolset, and have the swarm use it instead of reaching into a mutable list.

summary: Usage delta baseline resets across solver instances, duplicating previously recorded tokens in retry/resume traces
detail: The delta math reads the cumulative `cost_tracker.by_agent[self.agent_name]` (562) against per-instance baselines `_traced_input_tokens` etc. initialized to 0 (374-377). `agent_name` is only `f"{meta.name}/{self.model_id}"` (366) and the cost tracker is shared across solver instances: the early-exit retry re-queues the challenge (backend/agents/coordinator_core.py:131-141) and resume spawns a fresh swarm, so a second instance's first `_result` emits a usage event equal to ALL previously recorded tokens for that name. scripts/analyze_traces.py sums `usage` events per run, so retried/resumed runs report inflated costs.
fix_hint: Seed `_traced_*` from the current `by_agent` snapshot in `start()`, or emit usage events from the run's own `result.usage` delta instead of the globally cumulative value.

summary: Workdir slug is not injective and lets '.'/'..' through, so distinct challenges/models can share or escape the workspaces root
detail: swarm.py:115-116: re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+', '-', s).strip('-') or 'x'. Dot-only names survive: _slug('..') == '..', so _workdir_for (swarm.py:106-120) can resolve to <state_dir>/<model_spec> instead of <state_dir>/workspaces/<...>. The mapping is also lossy: 'A B' and 'A-B' (and 'a b' vs 'A-B' on case-insensitive Windows) collapse to one directory, as do model specs 'x/y' and 'x-y'; two different challenges/solvers then share one run_python cwd and TMP dir (local_exec.py:44-63) exactly where the prompt warns about cross-task contamination (prompts.py:167-169).
fix_hint: Make the component injective and safe: reject/short-circuit '.' and '..', normalise case, and append a short hash of the original string, e.g. f'{safe}-{sha1(original)[:8]}'.

summary: Budget floors can exceed the remaining global budget, contradicting the documented clamp
detail: swarm.py:66-67 clamps with max(60, min(limit, int(remaining_global_seconds))), so with 10s of run budget left a challenge is still granted 60s; _create_solver then computes time_budget = max(300, limit - 60) (swarm.py:132-137), so with 120s left the solver's own deadline (surfaced to the model via task_status, headless_solver.py:278-287) claims ~5 minutes. This contradicts the docstring at swarm.py:53-58 ('can never be handed a time limit longer than what is actually left of the WHOLE run').
fix_hint: Apply the 60s/300s floors only when the global budget is untracked; otherwise clamp after flooring: limit = min(limit, remaining) and budget = min(budget, remaining - margin).

summary: Solver creation happens outside the try and its failure is silently swallowed — a model can vanish with no log and a misleading 'finished' status
detail: _create_solver(model_spec) is called before the try block in _run_solver (swarm.py:295), so a failure inside it — e.g. _workdir_for's mkdir (swarm.py:118-119) on a Windows-reserved slug ('con', 'nul'), a >MAX_PATH path, or a permissions error — escapes the task; run() retrieves it via task.result() and does 'except Exception: continue' (swarm.py:449-451) without logging. The model simply disappears: no solver entry, get_status() shows it as 'finished' with 0 steps (swarm.py:496-506), and the operator gets no signal.
fix_hint: Wrap solver creation in the try (or catch and log it in run()), and harden _workdir_for against reserved/invalid directory names.

summary: Partial-stall watchdog ignores the pause state and withdraws an operator-paused multi-flag swarm
detail: The watchdog condition (swarm.py:410-414) looks only at _last_progress_monotonic and confirmed_flag; it never consults pause_event. While paused, _run_solver_loop stops starting solver turns (swarm.py:327-328), so no accepts happen; after partial_stall_seconds (default 600) the watchdog fires with reason 'stall_watchdog' (swarm.py:425), cancels the swarm and posts 'no new flag was accepted for 600s'. The coordinator then sees a swarm that ended without a result (coordinator_core.py:121-134), so an operator pause long enough to intervene can silently end the challenge.
fix_hint: Treat self.pause_event.is_set() as paused time in the watchdog (skip the check while paused and refresh _last_progress_monotonic on resume).

summary: get_status precedence makes the agent state 'won' unreachable and reports not-yet-started solvers as 'finished'.
detail: In get_status, `if self.cancel_event.is_set(): agent_status = "cancelled"` (backend/agents/swarm.py:498-499) is checked before `elif self.winner and self.winner.flag: agent_status = "won"` (L502-503), and every path that sets winner also sets cancel_event first (L340-341 sibling_win, L461-462 swarm_complete) — so the winning solver renders as 'cancelled' in the web console (backend/webui/index.html styles and status text) and the 'won' branch is dead. Relatedly, with no solver registered yet the chain falls through to the initial 'finished' (L497, L504-505), so a just-spawned swarm shows every agent as finished for the moment before its solvers start.
fix_hint: Check winner before cancel_event, and emit a distinct 'starting' state when solver is None and the swarm is neither cancelled nor paused.

summary: get_status() reports every agent of a solved swarm as 'cancelled'; the 'won' branch is unreachable
detail: swarm.py:498-505 checks cancel_event before winner, but winner is only assigned immediately after cancel_with_reason('sibling_win') (swarm.py:340-341), and run() likewise cancels before returning (swarm.py:453-457); when the task list drains it sets cancel_event 'swarm_complete' (swarm.py:461). Consequently a swarm that found a flag reports 'cancelled' for all agents (the winner included) and the 'won' branch at :502-503 can never be reached — affecting /status output (coordinator_loop.py:337-345) and the web console snapshot.
fix_hint: Check winner (terminal success) before the cancel/pause branches, or clear the cancelled display when winner is set.

summary: get_status()'s getattr(__getitem__) hack silently returns 0 for int-typed solvers and can raise KeyError for dict-typed ones
detail: swarm.py:507: getattr(getattr(solver, '_step_count', None), '__getitem__', lambda _: 0)(0). It works today only because HeadlessSolver._step_count is a one-element list cell (headless_solver.py:369); nothing in SolverProtocol (solver_base.py:20-33) requires that. An int-typed cell silently yields 0 steps/progress, and a dict-typed cell raises KeyError — swallowed in web.py:70-73 but unguarded in _print_status (coordinator_loop.py:341), where it would abort the scheduler event loop.
fix_hint: Give SolverProtocol a step_count property/field and read it directly; at minimum use getattr(solver, '_step_count', [0])[0].

summary: The model smoke test reports success when zero models were tested (`ok == len(results)` is 0 == 0).
detail: `model_specs = [s.strip() for s in model_specs if s.strip()]` (backend/cli.py:410) can empty the list (e.g. `--models ""`), so the loop runs no tests; then `ok = sum(...)` is 0 (L439) and `if ok == len(results):` prints the green '大模型 API Key 可正常调用。' (L442-443) above a '0/0 通过' line (L441), instead of failing loudly.
fix_hint: Guard for an empty model_specs list (fail with an error exit code) and require len(results) > 0 before declaring success.

summary: Write-only dataclass fields: HeadlessDeps.{cost_tracker,meta,use_vision,scenario,last_progress_step}, CoordinatorDeps.challenge_time_limit_seconds and ChallengeSwarm.challenge_dir
detail: Set but never read anywhere in the repo (grep-verified): deps.py:28 meta, :29 use_vision, :30 cost_tracker, :49 last_progress_step, :54 scenario (last_progress_step is written at headless_solver.py:239/297/532 and its comment describes a 'hint stall gate' that no longer exists); deps.py:66 challenge_time_limit_seconds is filled by build_deps (coordinator_loop.py:121-124) while every consumer reads settings.challenge_time_limit_seconds directly (swarm.py:60); swarm.py:75 challenge_dir is passed by all callers (coordinator_core.py:112, cli.py:289) and never read in swarm.py.
fix_hint: Delete the unused fields (or start reading them) so the dependency contracts stop advertising capability the code does not use.

summary: LoopDetector has no tests despite non-trivial signature/threshold logic
detail: `LoopDetector.check` (23+) builds sha1 signatures over full argument payloads, gates non-dict args, and drives the window/warn/break transitions consumed by the tracer. Nothing tests identical vs rotated arguments, the large-payload case the code comment explicitly calls out (the 500-char prefix truncation regression), empty args, or window eviction — a regression here would silently change loop telemetry for every solver run.
fix_hint: Unit-test threshold transitions (None -> warn -> break), window rollover, and full-args hashing including the long-shared-prefix case.

summary: Qwen URL/mode normalization and the spec parsing helpers are untested pure functions.
detail: resolve_model's qwen branch rewrites the base URL and api_mode with non-obvious rules ('/responses' suffix forces responses mode, '/chat/completions' forces chat, otherwise the setting wins — backend/models.py:88-107), and model_id_from_spec/provider_from_spec (L162-170) parse specs. All are pure and network-free; given that the shipped defaults already mismatch (see the qwen api_mode finding), table-driven tests would lock the intended behavior.
fix_hint: Add tests/test_models.py with cases for both URL suffixes, neither suffix, an invalid QWEN_API_MODE, and multi-segment specs.

detail: `effort_from_spec` (backend/models.py:173-176) and `context_window` (L186-188) plus the CONTEXT_WINDOWS table they feed (L49-54) have zero call sites anywhere in backend/ or scripts/ (grep-verified); VISION_MODELS (L57) is an empty set, so `supports_vision` (L181-183), which is still called at backend/agents/headless_solver.py:344, can only ever return False.

summary: Module docstring advertises a "local replay adapter" that does not exist after the rewrite.
detail: platforms.py:5 claims the TSecBench adapter "and the local replay adapter" implement the protocol, but there is exactly one implementation in the tree and no replay adapter is referenced anywhere else in the repo. It misstates the interface's real coverage for reviewers and for anyone adding a second backend.
fix_hint: Update the docstring to describe the single implementation (or state explicitly that the protocol is currently single-backend).

summary: SubmitResult.confirmed and PlatformIdentity are dead code — nothing in the repo references them.
detail: `confirmed` (lines 27-29) duplicates a membership test that swarm.py hand-rolls instead ("already_solved" at swarm.py:249, "correct" at swarm.py:256); a repo-wide search finds no `.confirmed` access. `PlatformIdentity` (lines 44-51) is referenced only by its own definition. Dead helpers invite drift: a status added to one place will not be reflected in the other.
fix_hint: Either use `result.confirmed` at the swarm call sites (and wire PlatformIdentity into a status display) or delete both before the upstream PR.

summary: The suspicious-data guard uses `// 2`, so it is a no-op for 1 known challenge and accepts responses that already lost half the list, which can wipe known state and trip the false 'all solved' exit.
detail: `if self._known_challenges and len(current_names) < len(self._known_challenges) // 2:` — with 1 known challenge the threshold is 0 and the check can never fire; with 3 known, a response containing 1 challenge passes. A single error response from `fetch_all_challenges` (which returns `[]` on any HTTP/parse error, tsec_platform.py:122-131) is then accepted and lines 135-136 overwrite `_known_challenges`/`_known_stubs` with the empty result; the solved-regression guard below cannot catch it when nothing is solved yet (`if self._known_solved and not current_solved` requires a previously non-empty solved set). With `known_challenges` emptied, the guard is permanently disabled and the scheduler's termination condition (coordinator_loop.py:299) declares 'All challenges solved' — the same silent-no-op failure as the seed case.
fix_hint: Use the literal 'fewer than half' test (`len(current_names) * 2 < len(self._known_challenges)`) and additionally treat any empty result as suspicious once a non-empty set was known (or when the adapter's fetch raised), never overwriting known state with a zero-length list.

summary: Module docstring contradicts the implementation and the function's own docstring about the target lock
detail: The module docstring says "`_guess_scenario` survives only to pick a per-challenge time budget and to gate the target lock" (7), but the lock is purely structural — `_target_lock_block` (headless_solver.py:101-134) matches `deps.allowed_hosts` parsed from `connection_info` and never consults `scenario` — and the function's own docstring at line 65 states the opposite: "never affects the target lock, which is purely structural". Two docstrings disagree; the module one is wrong.
fix_hint: Correct the module docstring to drop the target-lock claim (leave only the time-budget role).

summary: prompts.py docstring claims _guess_scenario is kept 'to gate the target lock'; the lock is purely structural and ignores it.
detail: The module docstring (lines 5-7) says the classifier 'survives only to pick a per-challenge time budget and to gate the target lock, never to shape the prompt text'. The budget use is real (swarm.py:62-65 gives killchain tasks a longer limit), but the lock is built solely from _parse_allowed_hosts and its own comment states 'no scenario/keyword guess can open it' (headless_solver.py:102-107); the deps.scenario field fed from line 362 is never read. Combined with the still-present keyword classifier, the docstring makes the removed behavior look load-bearing.
fix_hint: Correct the docstring to say the classifier only affects the time budget (or remove _guess_scenario in favor of a simple config knob), and delete the scenario plumbing.

summary: Prompt contract omits the flag shape that the rescue path depends on
detail: docs/rewrite-plan.md:93 requires the prompt to state "flag 形态与 `submit_flag` 语义", but `build_headless_prompt` lists only submit_flag semantics (153); the flag shape is never given. The solver's own fallback hard-assumes it: `_extract_flag_candidates` (headless_solver.py:51-58) and `_flag_inner` (66-70) only recognize `flag{...}`/`CTF{...}`, so for any task whose tokens use another shape the rescue silently finds nothing, and the model is never told the shape its fallback expects.
fix_hint: Add the expected flag shape (and that verbatim tokens must be submitted, not narrated) to the "## Constraints" block, or derive the rescue pattern from challenge metadata.

summary: do_submit_flag reports multi-flag partial credit as confirmed, ending the run early in the fallback submit path.
detail: `is_confirmed = result.status in ("correct", "already_solved")` ignores `challenge_complete`; tsec_platform.py:242-252 returns status 'correct' with challenge_complete=False for a partial multi-flag accept, and swarm.try_submit_flag deliberately returns confirmed=False in that case (swarm.py:256-266). Callers of the fallback (headless_solver.py:231-235 when deps.submit_fn is None, and the final-output rescue at 525-527) then set `ctx.deps.confirmed_flag`/`_confirmed`, so run_until_done_or_gave_up returns FLAG_FOUND (and in a swarm context triggers cancel_with_reason('sibling_win')) although flags remain unclaimed. Latent in today's wiring (swarm always injects submit_fn) but wrong for any standalone `HeadlessSolver(..., submit_fn=None)` use of this shared helper.
fix_hint: Mirror the swarm contract: is_confirmed = (status == 'already_solved') or (status == 'correct' and result.challenge_complete) (with a single-flag fallback when the platform omits totals), and add a test using a 2-flag partial accept.
evidence: Claim matches the code. core.py:12 `is_confirmed = result.status in ("correct", "already_solved")` ignores `challenge_complete`; tsec_platform.py:243-252 returns status `correct` with `complete = total_count > 0 and correct_count >= total_count` (False for a partial multi-flag accept), and swarm.py:259-270 deliberately returns confirmed=False in exactly that case (`if result.challenge_complete or not multi_flag: ... return result.display, False`). Fallback callers headless_solver.py:233-235 and 525-527 would set confirmed_flag/_confirmed and end the run as FLAG_FOUND with flags unclaimed. Latent: HeadlessSolver is constructed only at swarm.py:138, which always injects submit_fn (L145), so no in-repo path reaches the buggy fallback today - corrected to low.

summary: IMAGE_EXTS_FOR_VISION is unused despite the 'kept for prompt hints' comment.
detail: Repo-wide grep finds no consumer of IMAGE_EXTS_FOR_VISION (no prompts.py vision hint, and the related deps.use_vision flag is itself never read), so this table is dead code in an audited module — leftover from the removed vision/attachment path.
fix_hint: Delete the table (or implement the vision hint it presumes in prompts.build_headless_prompt and use it from there).

summary: The guard preamble is security-critical string codegen with zero tests.
detail: The preamble (49-70) is where every documented socket bypass lives (connect_ex, _socket.socket base class, UDP sendto, asyncio/Proactor on Windows, direct use of _orig_connect); nothing compiles it or asserts which API surface is wrapped. No test file exists in the repo despite pytest being declared in pyproject.
fix_hint: Generate the preamble in a test, exec it with a stub snippet, and assert that connect/connect_ex/create_connection/sendto are all guarded and that the original names are not reachable from user code.

summary: Non-connect egress paths (UDP sendto/sendmsg, DNS resolution helpers) escape the guard.
detail: `_guard` is only reached from the connect/create_connection wrappers; `socket.socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM).sendto(b'x', ('other-host', 53))` and `sendmsg` need no connect and reach arbitrary hosts, and `socket.gethostbyname`/`getaddrinfo`/`gethostbyaddr` issue resolver queries for arbitrary names (the audit's gethostbyname leak). This makes the function docstring's degraded claim ('localhost only', lines 35-37) and the solver's 'ALL outbound network access is locked' message inaccurate.
fix_hint: Wrap sendto/sendmsg with the same destination check (and consider allowing DNS only for allowed hosts, or explicitly documenting resolution as out of scope).

summary: run_python leaks the mkstemp fd every call, and the fallback cleanup silently never deletes the file on Windows.
detail: `Path(tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".py", prefix="agent_", dir=run_dir)[1])` discards the returned fd with no `os.close`, leaking one OS-level descriptor per tool call (long runs accumulate one per run_python invocation). On Windows the still-open handle makes `tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)` raise PermissionError (WinError 32), swallowed by the bare `except Exception: pass` at lines 128-130 — so the 'clean up the shared-temp fallback' path in the finally block never actually cleans up there.
fix_hint: `fd, name = tempfile.mkstemp(...); os.close(fd); tmp = Path(name)` before writing, so the handle is released and the fallback unlink works on Windows.

summary: Timeout kill only terminates the direct child; grandchildren keep running after the tool call returns.
detail: On timeout, `proc.kill()` kills just the spawned interpreter. Any process the snippet started (a background server, a long-running tool) survives, keeps ports/files and consumes host resources while the solver believes the call was killed. On POSIX the fix requires spawning with start_new_session=True and killing the group; on Windows TerminateProcess has no tree semantics either.
fix_hint: Spawn with start_new_session=True and on timeout signal the process group (os.killpg) on POSIX; on Windows use a job object or `taskkill /T` fallback.

summary: do_raw_http URL normalization and do_tcp_send framing/decode/truncation are untested.
detail: The scheme-prepend/lstrip rewrite (46-47 — the half of the empty-host lock bypass), the 24k truncation, follow_redirects behavior, and _decode_payload's hex-over-payload precedence have no tests anywhere in the repo (pyproject declares pytest but no test files exist). A test asserting that a host-less URL is rejected, or that redirects are re-checked, would have caught the findings above.
fix_hint: Add unit tests using an httpx MockTransport for URL handling/redirect policy, and direct tests for _truncate/_decode_payload and the read-loop deadline.

summary: _sanitize strips only '/' and ' ', so Windows-hostile characters in a challenge or model id make the tracer constructor raise.
detail: `_sanitize` replaces only '/' and ' ' (backend/tracing.py:11-12) and the resulting name is opened unguarded in __init__ (`self._fh = open(self.path, "a")`, L22) at logs/trace-{challenge}-{model_id}-{ts}.jsonl (L21). On Windows ':' is illegal in file names and '\' is a path separator; a model id with a ':' suffix (a real naming style — see genai-prices ids like 'qwen/qwen-plus-2025-07-28:thinking') or any backslash in the challenge name raises OSError/FileNotFoundError inside HeadlessSolver.__init__ (construction at backend/agents/headless_solver.py:365), taking down the solver rather than just its trace file.
fix_hint: Whitelist sanitize ([A-Za-z0-9._-]) and wrap the open in try/except with a fallback filename, so tracing can never fail a solver spawn.

summary: tool_call serializes args outside the tracer's exception guard, and all truncations are silent.
detail: `args_str = args if isinstance(args, str) else json.dumps(args)` (backend/tracing.py:43) runs before `_write`'s try/except (L35-40) — the guard exists precisely so tracing failures cannot break the solver, yet this one line can raise (non-JSON-serializable values such as bytes/Decimal in tool args) into the solver's tool path. Additionally, args are cut at 2000 chars, results at 2000 and model text at 1000 (L44, L47, L50) with no `truncated` marker, so scripts/analyze_traces.py cannot distinguish a complete payload from a truncated one.
fix_hint: Move the serialization inside _write (e.g. json.dumps(..., default=str) wrapped in the same try) and add a `truncated: true` flag when the payload is cut.

summary: Challenge and solved caches are only ever added to, never reconciled with the newest listing.
detail: `fetch_all_challenges` writes into `_challenge_index` (line 156) and `_solved_cache` (158-159) but never removes entries missing from the newest payload, and `fetch_solved_names` answers from the cache without refetching once the index is populated (163-166). A long-lived adapter can therefore resolve submit_flag/release_challenge/fetch_hint lookups (182-193, 307-316, 266-275) for a challenge that no longer exists to a stale unique_code, and can report a stale solved set. Impact is latent in a single-round process (the poller path always refetches via fetch_poll_state), but the state is wrong by construction.
fix_hint: Rebuild `_challenge_index` from scratch on each fetch (and drop `_solved_cache` names absent from the payload).

summary: Both retry loops sleep after their final failed attempt and log incorrect attempt counters.
detail: start_challenge's `range(6)` (line 331) still sleeps up to 14s after the 6th failed 409 (line 350) before falling through to the raise (353-354), and its "(x/5)" message (347-348) can print "(6/5)". close_challenge's `range(4)` (line 371) likewise sleeps 15s after the 4th failure (387/394) before raising (395-396), and `min(attempt + 1, 3)` makes attempts 3 and 4 both log "(3/3)" (384-385, 391-392). The dead waits run on the teardown/failure path where the slot is still held.
fix_hint: Skip the sleep on the final iteration and report attempt counts from the actual loop bound without the min() clamp.

summary: Retry and fatal-state classification hinge on untested, unversioned human-readable message substrings with no shared constants.
detail: The only trigger for the capacity backoff is `409 and "max active" in body` (line 344); the only trigger for surfacing a dead task is `"already finished" in body or "task_not_found" in body` (lines 122-123). These prose substrings are the entire coupling to platform semantics. If the server rewords a message, the start path silently stops waiting (spawn failures escalate to deferrals instead of retrying) and the fatal-state guard degrades a finished task into a swallowed empty list — the exact failure mode the guard exists to prevent. Nothing pins these strings: no constants, no fixtures, no tests.
fix_hint: Prefer structured `code` fields from the JSON error body, extract shared constants, and pin them with recorded fixtures.

summary: Cached container addresses are reused with no freshness check, so a recycled or closed range can be handed to a solver as its target.
detail: The reuse branch (lines 420-423) prefers `_started_addrs` whenever the fresh challenge dict has no addr, ignoring the freshly fetched `container_status` (normalized at line 151) and applying no TTL. Entries are removed only on a successful close (line 397), so after an invalid/failed close or a platform-side recycle the cached address is served as `connection_info`; the solver burns budget on an unreachable target, and the coordinator's early-exit retry re-pulls into the same cached entry instead of revalidating. Compounds with the close-4xx defect above (entry never popped on the raise path).
fix_hint: Only reuse when the fresh listing still reports container_status == "available"; otherwise delete the entry and go through start+poll.

summary: The websocket out queue is unbounded while the pusher enqueues a full snapshot every second regardless of client backpressure.
detail: `out: asyncio.Queue = asyncio.Queue()` (backend/web.py:160) has no maxsize; pusher unconditionally put_nowait's `{"type": "state", **build_snapshot(...)}` every 1.0 s (L164-167) while sender drains it (L169-172). If a client stalls (throttled tab, slow link), the queue grows without bound — each message contains every challenge and every swarm's status — until the socket is eventually closed.
fix_hint: Use maxsize=1 with drop-oldest semantics for state pushes (or skip enqueuing when the previous state message is still pending); keep the lossless path only for trace events.

summary: The server-side `watching` variable is assigned but never read.
detail: `watching: tuple[str, str] | None = None` (backend/web.py:162) is set on watch (L199), cleared on unwatch (L210), and resurrected only as `_ = watching` at L222 purely to silence linters — it carries no state used by the tail/snapshot logic.
fix_hint: Remove the variable (and the `_ = watching` line), or actually use it (e.g. include the current watch target in build_snapshot output).

summary: The console's status filter list lacks 'preparing' although the server emits that status, so preparing challenges vanish under every non-'all' filter.
detail: STATUSES = ["all","active","deferred","unsolved","solved"] (backend/webui/index.html:201) while the snapshot produces 'preparing' (backend/web.py:34-44 `_challenge_status` returns it for names in deps.pending_spawns). The local rank table knows the status (index.html:225 `{ active:0, preparing:1, ... }`) but the filter is `c.status === filter` (L227), so a challenge being started is only visible under 'all'.
fix_hint: Add "preparing" to STATUSES so it gets a filter button and stays visible while spawning.

summary: Platform-provided value/level/status are interpolated into innerHTML without esc(), unlike name/category.
detail: The challenge row builds `...${c.value||0} 分${c.level?` · L${c.level}`:''}...` and `class="pill ${c.status}"` raw (backend/webui/index.html:236-237) while name and category are escaped with esc() (L235/L237, helper at L345). Those fields are passed through verbatim from the TSecBench API response (`stub.get("value", 0)` / `stub.get("level", 0)` / server-computed status, backend/web.py:57-65), so a malformed or crafted platform payload can inject markup/script into the operator console.
fix_hint: Wrap every interpolation in esc() (a numeric coercion for value/level would also do), keeping one consistent escaping rule for the whole row.

summary: onTrace has no fallback branch, so several events the solver emits never appear in the watch panel.
detail: The if/else chain (backend/webui/index.html:309-319) covers tool_call/tool_result/flag_confirmed/error/usage/bump/finish/start/model_response/loop_detected, but the solver also emits target_lock_block (backend/agents/headless_solver.py:162-166 and 185-189), target_lock_degraded (L395-400) and findings_injected (backend/agents/tracing_toolset.py:65) — events with no branch are silently dropped, so the operator watching a solver cannot see that egress was refused by the target lock, which is a core steering signal in this codebase.
fix_hint: Add a final `else addEv("meta", ev.type || "event", trunc(JSON.stringify(stripTs(ev))), ev.step)` so unknown event types are visible instead of invisible.

summary: _SCENARIO_WORDS claims it is kept in sync with prompts.py::_guess_scenario but has drifted, mis-classifying exploit-type runs as 'web'.
detail: backend/prompts.py:76-77 maps 挖掘/审计/安全测试/cve and comfyui/gradio/ollama/dify to 'exploit'; the copy at scripts/analyze_traces.py:54-66 stops after ('rce','poc','利用','exp_') at L58, so runs whose only signals are those words fall through to the default 'web' (guess_scenario, L69, applied at L276), skewing the per-scenario rate tables even though the comment above the tuple says 'kept in sync manually' (L51-52).
fix_hint: Import the classifier from backend.prompts (the package is importable) or delete the manual copy so there is one word table.
